data.about: The Golden Gate Bridge as a chain of graphic-statics constructions: the main cable is the funicular of 29 equal hanger loads, its pole found from the half-chords of the draggable sag point; the towers must be balanced horizontally, so the backstay cables share the same horizontal component H — their poles lie on the vertical at distance H from the side load line, located with a trial funicular. Tower tops carry the vertical resultants E = A + C and F = B + D, and the anchor blocks resist the cable pulls with components H_H, H_V and J_H, J_V.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the roadway between two towers and two anchor blocks — main span 4200 ft, side spans 1125 ft; the deck hangs from 29 + 8 + 8 hangers (drag the anchor point)
steps.title: Site: the Golden Gate Bridge

steps.caption: left: the main-span deck loads the cable with 29 equal hanger loads P, resultant R₁ at midspan — right: the load line R₁ (field), 29 pieces
steps.title: The main-span load R₁

steps.caption: left: the half-chords from the sag point (drag it) to the tower tops — right: parallels to them through the division points i₁, i₂ of each half-span load meet at the pole o (toggle "trial construction" to see why)
steps.title: Half-chords → the pole o

steps.caption: right: rays from o to every cut — left: the funicular of the 29 hanger loads through the sag point lands exactly on both tower tops; the hangers drop to the deck
steps.title: The main cable

steps.caption: right: the outer rays are the cable end forces A and B — left: the same pulls at the tower tops, along the end tangents
steps.title: Cable forces A and B

steps.caption: both: A and B split into the horizontal pull A_H = B_H = H and the vertical parts A_V = B_V (half the main load each)
steps.title: Components of A and B

steps.caption: left: each side span loads its backstay cable with 8 hanger loads P, resultant R₂ — right: the side load line R₂ (side), 8 pieces
steps.title: The side-span load R₂

steps.caption: left: a trial funicular (grey) closes the side span, its division point i₃ + the chord anchor–tower — right: the parallel to the chord through i₃ meets the vertical at distance H (the tower must be balanced: C_H = A_H) at the pole o₁
steps.title: Same H → the side pole o₁

steps.caption: right: rays from o₁ — left: the side-span funicular from the anchorage to the tower top; the force triangle closes with the anchor pull H and the backstay force C
steps.title: The backstay cable — H and C

steps.caption: left: mirrored about midspan: cable, hangers and R₂ — right: the mirrored pole o₂ gives the forces D (backstay) and J (anchor pull)
steps.title: The right side span

steps.caption: right: tip-to-tail, A and C (and mirrored B and D) sum to a vertical: E = A_V + C_V, F = B_V + D_V — left: the towers push up under the deck
steps.title: Tower equilibrium: E and F

steps.caption: both: the anchor blocks resist the cable pulls with the components H_H, H_V and J_H, J_V — the horizontal pull H_H equals H again
steps.title: Anchor forces

steps.caption: the cables and hangers resolve pink = tension, the towers blue = compression; forces in units of the hanger load P on the right
steps.title: Tension and compression
